task.description: CODE-DESIGNER pass (WF-02 Step 1) for REQ-194 (queue task 367, GH#713): design a Prometheus metrics subsystem (OBS-02) resolving REQ-078's three recorded divergences (auth, scope, format) against fresh evidence that web/src/api/metrics.ts already expects Prometheus text from an unversioned GET /metrics. Read REQ-078's placeholder (lib/letflow/routers/metrics.ex), confirm zero real :telemetry.execute call sites and no metrics dependency in mix.exs, reach explicit stated positions on all three axes (format settled by the SPA evidence; auth/scope reasoned through independently, including whether a definition_id-style label can leak cross-tenant identifiers on a global endpoint), decide on a metrics dependency vs hand-rolled registry (flagging REVIEWER sign-off if a dependency is added, mirroring REQ-148's tv-labs/lua precedent), specify the six OBS-02 metric families' :telemetry event/measurement/metadata shapes, the route-template normalization rule for HTTP labels, the exposition endpoint's exact path/format/Content-Type/auth, DB-unavailable graceful degradation plus a staleness decision, and the disposition of lib/letflow/routers/metrics.ex. Design only -- @spec/@type/interface descriptions, zero implementation code.
acceptance_criteria: this requirement states an explicit decision on each of REQ-078's three recorded divergences -- auth, scope and format -- with a reason for each, in the module moduledoc; it does not silently pick one or leave any of the three unstated

the format decision cites web/src/api/metrics.ts's parsePrometheusText and metricsApi.prometheusText()'s call to client.getText('/metrics') as an already-committed consumer contract, and the endpoint Letflow serves is one that web/src/pages/admin/MetricsPage.tsx actually reaches -- asserted by a test hitting that exact path

if a metrics dependency is added to mix.exs, REVIEWER sign-off is recorded for it in this requirement's PR; if instead a registry is hand-rolled, the moduledoc states that as the decision -- one or the other, not silence

all six OBS-02 core metric families are present in the exposition output after exercising the corresponding behaviour, asserted by parsing the response body -- not by asserting the emission call was made

the HTTP-request metric labels by route template and not by raw path: two requests to the same route with different path parameters produce ONE label combination, not two, asserted by counting distinct label sets in the output

the auth and scope decisions are enforced and tested: whichever position was taken, a test asserts that one tenant's scrape cannot observe another tenant's figures or identifiers (including through label values), or -- if the endpoint is deliberately global and unauthenticated -- that no metric label carries any tenant-identifying value at all
the exposition endpoint returns a successful response with the last known values when the database is unavailable, rather than erroring, asserted with the database made unreachable

instrumentation is emitted via :telemetry events and the registry attaches to them, so the emitting call sites do not reference the registry module directly, confirmed by grep over the instrumented modules
the disposition of lib/letflow/routers/metrics.ex is explicit -- removed, or retained with its role stated in its own moduledoc -- and no route the SPA calls returns 404 afterwards
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

result.summary: Design produced at lib/letflow/design/req194-prometheus-metrics.md, design-only (@spec/@type/interface tables and prose, zero literal Elixir implementation code -- every fenced block contains only @spec/@type declarations, verified by inspection). AXIS 1 (format): settled by direct evidence -- web/src/api/metrics.ts's parsePrometheusText and metricsApi.prometheusText()'s client.getText('/metrics') (unversioned, top-level) are an already-committed consumer contract; decision is Prometheus exposition text, Content-Type 'text/plain; version=0.0.4', at GET /metrics outside /api/v1. AXIS 2/3 (auth+scope, decided together): global and unauthenticated (mounted at Letflow.Router's top tier alongside /health and /api/tenant-config, outside ApiPipeline/AuthPipeline), reasoned through REQ-078's own substantive tenant-exposure concern rather than picking either precedent wholesale -- resolved by moving the protection from 'authenticate + scope the query' (incompatible with a genuine global scrape target, since :MetricsRead is unconditionally :Allow per authorization.ex) to a structural label-allowlist invariant: no metric family's label set ever carries a tenant_id/definition_id/instance_id/task_id/actor_id, enforced per-family by each :telemetry handler extracting only a fixed, hand-built key set (mirroring metrics.ex's own counter_group/2 discipline). The 'task-completions by definition' family is explicitly restated (named as a restatement, precedented by decision 0014's LUA-01/WASM-10 pattern) to label by definition_status (draft/active/deprecated/archived, a closed 4-value enum) rather than definition_id/name, since a raw identifier is exactly what the global/unauthenticated shape forbids. DEPENDENCY DECISION: no telemetry_metrics/telemetry_metrics_prometheus_core added -- hand-rolled Letflow.Metrics.Registry (ETS-backed, GenServer-owned table, direct-from-caller-process :ets updates so metric emission never blocks on a GenServer mailbox) and Letflow.Metrics.Exposition (pure text formatter). One mix.exs change is proposed and FLAGGED PROMINENTLY FOR REVIEWER SIGN-OFF: an explicit {:telemetry, "~> 1.4"} deps/0 line -- telemetry v1.4.2 is already fetched/compiled/running transitively via bandit/db_connection/ecto/ecto_sql/plug (confirmed in mix.lock and deps/), so this adds zero new bytes/transitive tree, but per REQ-194's own AC3 (no size-based carve-out stated) this design does not unilaterally decide the exception applies to itself, mirroring REQ-148's tv-labs/lua sign-off precedent even though the risk profile is materially smaller. Six metric families fully specified (Section 3): letflow_active_instances (gauge, periodic scheduler-driven refresh, DB-unavailable-safe) plus a companion _last_refresh_timestamp_seconds staleness gauge (Letflow DOES expose staleness, unlike R-Co's recorded honest gap); letflow_task_completions_total (counter, definition_status label); letflow_event_append_duration_seconds (histogram, via a new :telemetry.span/3 wrap of EventStore.append/2's existing Repo.transaction call -- no existing hook to attach to); letflow_db_query_duration_seconds (histogram, query_type label, attaches to Ecto's OWN already-emitted [:letflow, :repo, :query] telemetry event -- zero new instrumentation call site, confirmed by reading deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql.ex:900-1315 and deps/ecto/lib/ecto/repo/supervisor.ex:55-59 for the default telemetry_prefix); letflow_http_requests_total and letflow_http_errors_total (counters, method/route_template/status and route_template respectively, from a new Letflow.Plugs.HttpMetrics plug). Route-template normalization rule (Section 2) uses Plug.Router.match_path/1 (deps/plug/lib/plug/router.ex:324-327) reading conn.private[:plug_route], which append_match_path/2 (same file, 520-528) already composes across a forward()-ed sub-router into the full literal template (e.g. '/api/v1/instances/:id') -- no custom regex needed; unmatched requests fall back to the bounded constant 'unmatched', never the raw path. DB-unavailable graceful degradation (Section 6): only the active-instances gauge touches Repo (via Letflow.Scheduler.Poller's tick, extending the same GenServer that already runs REQ-188's retention sweep -- no new periodic child, per ORD-04's own established precedent); a caught DBConnection.ConnectionError on that refresh step never crashes the Poller (which would stop firing timers platform-wide) and simply leaves the gauge/timestamp at their last successful values; the exposition endpoint itself never touches Repo for any of the other five families. Disposition of lib/letflow/routers/metrics.ex (Section 9): REMOVED entirely (its own moduledoc has said since REQ-078 it is a placeholder pending supersession); its forward/2 mount in api_pipeline.ex:66 removed; the SPA never called /api/v1/metrics in the first place (REQ-078's own moduledoc recorded this as known breakage), so nothing the SPA calls regresses -- GET /metrics starts working for the first time instead of 404ing. :MetricsRead's leftover presence in Authorization is named as an explicit open question (Section 10), not silently pruned, since enum-member removal is cross-cutting and outside this requirement's stated scope item 5. Full traceability table (Section 11) maps all 10 real docs/requirements.yaml acceptance criteria to concrete design elements. Section 12 names 4 open questions explicitly (MetricsRead cleanup, bucket-boundary configurability, exact definition_status binding reuse point in complete_task/3, refresh-cadence granularity) rather than leaving them implicit.
